variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,    # parameters   threshold, epsilon, lambda,    # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   # epsilon-first   if (i <= threshold) {     try <- 1   } else if (i > threshold & is.na(epsilon) & is.na(lambda)) {     try <- 0   # epsilon-greedy   } else if (i > threshold & !(is.na(epsilon)) & is.na(lambda)){     try <- sample(       c(1, 0),       prob = c(epsilon, 1 - epsilon),       size = 1     )   # epsilon-decreasing   } else if (i > threshold & is.na(epsilon) & !(is.na(lambda))) {     try <- sample(       c(1, 0),       prob = c(         1 / (1 + lambda * i),          lambda * i / (1 + lambda * i)       ),       size = 1     )   }   # error   else {     try <- "ERROR"   }      return(try) } print(binaryRL::func_pi) func_pi <- function(   # variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,   # adjusting Left option value or Right option  value   LR,   # parameters   pi,    # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   # at least 1   if (is.na(x = pi)) {     if (L_pick == 0 & R_pick == 0) {       bias <- 0     }     else if (LR == "L" & L_pick == 0 & R_pick > 0) {       bias <- 1e+4     }     else if (LR == "R" & R_pick == 0 & L_pick > 0) {       bias <- 1e+4     }     else {       bias <- 0     }   }   # bias value   else if (!(is.na(x = pi)) & LR == "L") {     bias <- pi * sqrt(log(L_pick + exp(1)) / (L_pick + 1e-10))   }   else if (!(is.na(x = pi)) & LR == "R") {     bias <- pi * sqrt(log(R_pick + exp(1)) / (R_pick + 1e-10))   }   # error   else {     bias <- "ERROR"   }    return(bias) } print(binaryRL::func_tau) func_tau <- function (   # variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,    # Exploration–Exploitation Trade-off      try,   # calculating Left option or Right option probability   LR,   # parameters   lapse,   tau,    # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   # random   if (try == 1) {     prob <- 0.5   }    # greedy-max   else if (try == 0 & LR == "L" & is.na(tau)) {     if (L_value == R_value) {       prob <- 0.5     }      else if (L_value > R_value) {       prob <- 1     }     else if (L_value < R_value) {       prob <- 0     }   }   else if (try == 0 & LR == "R" & is.na(tau)) {     if (L_value == R_value) {       prob <- 0.5     }      else if (R_value > L_value) {       prob <- 1     }     else if (R_value < L_value) {       prob <- 0     }   }   # soft-max   else if (try == 0 & LR == "L" & !(is.na(tau))) {     prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(L_value - R_value) * tau))   }   else if (try == 0 & LR == "R" & !(is.na(tau))) {     prob <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(R_value - L_value) * tau))   }   # error   else {     prob <- "ERROR"   }      prob <- (1 - lapse) * prob + (lapse / 2)      return(prob) } print(binaryRL::func_logl) func_logl <- function(   # variables before decision-making   i, L_freq, R_freq, L_pick, R_pick, L_value, R_value,    # variables after decision-making   value, utility, reward, occurrence,   # Whether the participant chose the left or right option.   L_dir, R_dir,    # The probability that the model assigns to choosing the left or right option   L_prob, R_prob,        # Exploration–Exploitation Trade-off      try,   # calculating Left option logl or Right option logl   LR,      # extra variables   var1, var2,    # extra parameters   alpha, beta  ){   logl <- switch(     EXPR = LR,     "L" = L_dir * log(L_prob),     "R" = R_dir * log(R_prob)   )      return(logl)   }

title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
text: Create model function accepts parm Data arguments, return value conforms structure required LaplacesDemon. Within function, need calculate sum log-likelihoods sum log-posteriors across subjects using specified prior distributions.
code: Model <- function(parm, Data) {      # Initialize accumulators for sum of log-likelihood and log-posterior   sum_LL <- 0   sum_LP <- 0      # Loop through each subject ID provided in the Data list   for (i in as.vector(Data$id)) {          # read unconstrained params     eta_unconstrained <- parm[(i - 1) * 2 + 1]     tau_unconstrained <- parm[(i - 1) * 2 + 2]          # convert to constrained params     eta <- stats::plogis(eta_unconstrained)     tau <- exp(tau_unconstrained)          # pass constrained params to the input vector     #parm[(i - 1) * 2 + 1] <- eta     #parm[(i - 1) * 2 + 2] <- tau          res <- binaryRL::run_m(       data = Data$df,       id = Data$id[i],       eta = eta,       tau = tau,       priors = Data$priors,       n_params = Data$n_params,       n_trials = Data$n_trials,       mode = Data$mode,       policy = Data$policy     )          # Add the log-likelihood of the current subject to the total     sum_LL <- sum_LL + res$ll     # Add the log-posterior of the current subject to the total     LP_eta <- stats::dnorm(x = eta, mean = 0.5, sd = 0.15, log = TRUE)     LP_tau <- stats::dexp(x = tau, rate = 1, log = TRUE)     sum_LP <- sum_LP + LP_eta + LP_tau   }      LP <- sum_LL + sum_LP      # Return a list in the format required by LaplacesDemon   return(     list(       LP = LP,       Dev = -2 * sum_LL,       Monitor = c(LP = LP),       yhat = NULL,       parm = parm     )   ) }

Critically, uses probabilities     sample action. value update performed action     model selected. approach focuses directly     mimicking stochastic choice patterns agent, rather just     learning underlying values fixed sequence actions. default: policy = "" estimate [string] Estimation method. Can either "MLE" "MAP". "MLE": (Default) Maximum Likelihood Estimation.       method finds parameter values maximize log-likelihood       data. higher log-likelihood indicates parameters       provide better explanation observed human behavior.       words, data simulated using parameters       closely resemble actual human data. method       consider prior information parameters. "MAP": Maximum Posteriori Estimation. method       finds parameter values maximize posterior probability.       iterative process based Expectation-Maximization       (EM) framework. Initialization: process begins assuming           uniform distribution prior parameter, making           initial log-prior zero. first optimization thus           equivalent MLE. Iteration: finding best parameters           subjects, algorithm assesses actual distribution           parameter fits normal distribution .           fitted distribution becomes new empirical prior. Re-estimation: parameters re-optimized           maximize updated posterior probability. Convergence: cycle repeats posterior           probability converges maximum number iterations           (specified iteration_g) reached. default: estimate = "MLE" data [data.frame] data include following mandatory columns: sub "Subject" time_line "Block" "Trial" L_choice "L_choice" R_choice "R_choice" L_reward "L_reward" R_reward "R_reward" sub_choose "Sub_Choose" id [CharacterVector] vector specifying subject ID(s) parameters   fitted. function process subjects provided   vector. fit subjects, can either explicitly set argument   id = unique(data$Subject) leave default   (id = NULL). approaches direct function fit   parameters every unique subject dataset. strongly recommended avoid using simple numeric sequences like   id = 1:4. practice can lead errors subject IDs   stored strings (e.g., subject four stored "004")   sequentially numbered. default: id = NULL n_trials [integer] Represents total number trials single subject experienced  experiment. parameter kept default value  NULL, program automatically detect many trials  subject experienced provided data. information  primarily used calculating model fit statistics  AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) BIC (Bayesian Information  Criterion). default: n_trials = NULL funcs [CharacterVector] character vector containing names user-defined functions  required computation. parallel computation enabled  (.e., nc > 1), user-defined models custom functions  might automatically accessible within parallel environment. Therefore, created reinforcement learning model  modifies package's default six default functions  (default functions:     util_func = func_gamma,     rate_func = func_eta,     expl_func = func_epsilon,     bias_func = func_pi,     prob_func = func_tau,     loss_func = func_logl  ),  must explicitly provide names custom functions  vector . model_name [List] name fit modals e.g. model_name = c("TD", "RSTD", "Utility") fit_model [List] collection functions applied fit models data. e.g. fit_model = list(binaryRL::TD, binaryRL::RSTD, binaryRL::Utility) lower [List] lower bounds model fit models e.g. lower = list(c(0, 0), c(0, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 0)) upper [List] upper bounds model fit models e.g. upper = list(c(1, 10), c(1, 1, 10), c(1, 1, 10)) priors [List] list specifying prior distributions model parameters.   argument mandatory using estimate = "MAP".   two primary scenarios use: 1. Static MAP Estimation (Non-Hierarchical)   approach used strong, pre-defined belief   parameter priors want model update iteratively. Configuration:  Set estimate = "MAP". Provide list defining confident prior           distributions. Keep iteration_g = 0 (default).  Behavior: algorithm maximizes posterior       probability based solely specified priors.       use EM (Expectation-Maximization) framework learn new       priors data. 2. Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation via EM   approach used let model learn group-level (hierarchical)   prior distributions directly data. Configuration:  Set estimate = "MAP". Specify weak non-informative initial prior,           uniform distribution parameters. Set iteration_g value greater 0.  Behavior: uniform prior, initial       log-posterior equals log-likelihood, making first estimation       step equivalent MLE. algorithm initiates EM procedure:       iteratively assesses actual parameter distribution across       subjects updates group-level priors. cycle continues       posterior converges iteration_g reached. default: priors = NULL tolerance [double] Convergence threshold MAP estimation. change  log posterior probability iterations smaller value,  algorithm considered converged program stop. default: tolerance = 0.001 iteration_i [integer] number iterations optimization algorithm perform  searching best-fitting parameters fitting  phase. higher number iterations may increase likelihood  finding global optimum also increases computation time. default: iteration_i = 10. iteration_g [integer] maximum number iterations Expectation-Maximization (EM)  based MAP estimation. algorithm stop iteration  count reached, even change log-posterior value  yet fallen tolerance threshold. default: iteration_g = 0. initial_params [NumericVector] Initial values free parameters optimization algorithm  search . primarily relevant using algorithms require  explicit starting point, L-BFGS-B. specified,  function automatically generate initial values close zero. default: initial_params = NA. initial_size [integer] parameter corresponds population size genetic  algorithms (GA). specifies number initial candidate  solutions algorithm starts evolutionary search.  parameter required optimization algorithms operate  population, GA DEoptim. default: initial_size = 50. seed [integer] Random seed. ensures results  reproducible remain time function run. default: seed = 123 nc [integer] Number cores use parallel processing. code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ func_epsilon <- function(   # Trial number   i,   # Number of times this option has appeared   L_freq,   R_freq,   # Number of times this option has been chosen   L_pick,   R_pick,   # Current value of this option   L_value,   R_value,   # Extra variables   var1 = NA,   var2 = NA,      # Free Parameters   threshold = 1,   epsilon = NA,   lambda = NA,   # Extra parameters   alpha,   beta ){   # Epsilon-First: random choosing before a certain trial number   if (i <= threshold) {     try <- 1   } else if (i > threshold & is.na(epsilon) & is.na(lambda)) {     try <- 0   # Epsilon-Greedy: random choosing throughout the experiment with probability epsilon   } else if (i > threshold & !(is.na(epsilon)) & is.na(lambda)){     try <- sample(       c(1, 0),       prob = c(epsilon, 1 - epsilon),       size = 1     )   # Epsilon-Decreasing: probability of random choosing decreases as trials increase   } else if (i > threshold & is.na(epsilon) & !(is.na(lambda))) {     try <- sample(       c(1, 0),       prob = c(         1 / (1 + lambda * i),         lambda * i / (1 + lambda * i)       ),       size = 1     )   }   else {     try <- "ERROR"   }    return(try) } } # }
